rule: Pages with no title. Give every page its own `<title>`; Google often uses it as the link in search results.
formula: no <title> text

rule: Pages that share their title with another page. Give each page its own title, so search results can tell them apart.
formula: same title on two or more pages

rule: Titles longer than 60 characters. Put the words that matter first: search results usually cut long titles off.
formula: len(title) > TITLE_MAX_CHARS
notes: Google sets no length limit; it truncates by pixel width, which about 60 characters fits.

rule: Pages with no meta description. Write a sentence or two; Google sometimes shows it under the link.
formula: no meta description

rule: Pages that share their meta description. Describe each page in its own words, or leave it out and let Google choose.
formula: same meta description on two or more pages

rule: Pages with no main heading (`<h1>`). Give each page one visible main heading that matches its topic.
formula: no <h1>
notes: Not a Google requirement; a heading structure helps screen readers (WCAG 1.3.1).

rule: Pages with images that have no alt text. Add an `alt` to every image: describe it, or use `alt=""` if it's decoration. Screen readers and search engines read it.
formula: an with no alt attribute

rule: Pages with no language set. Set it on the page, e.g. `<html lang="en">`; screen readers and translation use it.
formula: no lang on <html>

rule: Pages with no mobile viewport. Add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` so phones don't show a shrunken desktop page.
formula: no meta viewport

rule: Pages that redirect with a meta refresh. Use a server redirect instead; search engines and screen readers handle it better.
formula: a meta http-equiv=refresh

rule: URLs that redirect 2 or more times in a row. Point the first URL straight at the final one.
formula: redirect hops >= REDIRECT_CHAIN_HOPS

rule: Internal links that point at a redirect. Link to the final URL, so visitors and crawlers skip the extra hop.
formula: an internal link whose URL redirects

rule: Broken internal links. Fix or remove links to pages that don't exist: each one is a dead end.
formula: an internal URL answers 4xx or 5xx

rule: Broken links to other sites. Update or remove them.
formula: an external URL answers 404, 410, 5xx or nothing; these refusals don't count
notes: Sites that refuse bots (LinkedIn's 999, Cloudflare's 403) are listed apart as unverified, not broken.

rule: Links to other sites that refuse automated checks. Nothing to fix unless one looks wrong: these sites block bots, so check by hand.
formula: an external URL answers one of the refusal codes

rule: Pages that couldn't be fetched. Check that they load: slow or failing pages lose visitors and crawlers.
formula: no response, a bot wall, or a body past the size limit

rule: Missing pages that answer `200 OK`. Answer a page that doesn't exist with a real `404`, or search engines may index the error page.
formula: a made-up URL answers 200

rule: The home page is hidden from search engines. Remove the noindex, or the robots.txt rule that blocks it, unless the site is meant to be hidden.
formula: the home page is noindex or disallowed by robots.txt

rule: robots.txt answers with a server error, or not at all. Make it answer normally (or with `404` if you don't need one): while it fails, Google stops crawling the site.
formula: robots.txt answers 5xx or nothing
notes: Google treats a robots.txt that fails with a server error as disallowing the whole site, after a grace period.

rule: No robots.txt. Optional: add one, if only to point crawlers at your sitemap.
formula: robots.txt answers 4xx

rule: No readable XML sitemap. Publish one at `/sitemap.xml`, or list it in robots.txt, so search engines find every page.
formula: no sitemap read from robots.txt or /sitemap.xml

rule: Sitemap URLs that aren't indexable pages. List only final pages that load and may be indexed: no redirects, errors, noindex pages or pages robots.txt blocks.
formula: a sitemap URL that redirects, fails, is noindex or is blocked

rule: Pages that ask search engines not to index them. Check each one is meant to stay out of search results.
formula: meta robots or X-Robots-Tag noindex

rule: Pages with more than one canonical. Keep a single `rel=canonical`; with several, Google ignores them.
formula: more than one distinct rel=canonical

rule: Canonicals that point at a page that can't be indexed. Point the canonical at the final, indexable version of the page.
formula: the canonical target redirects, fails, is noindex or is blocked

rule: Pages with JSON-LD that isn't valid JSON. Fix the syntax: search engines skip a block they can't parse.
formula: a JSON-LD block that doesn't parse

rule: Structured data missing a property Google requires. Add the property named next to each page; without it the item can't get a rich result.
formula: a typed item missing one of Google's required properties for its rich result
notes: Covers Product, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage, Event, LocalBusiness, Recipe, JobPosting, Review and VideoObject; the full rules are in Google's Rich Results Test.

rule: The home page has no structured data. Describe the business with Organization or LocalBusiness markup in JSON-LD.
formula: no JSON-LD or microdata on the home page

rule: Pages with no Open Graph title or image. Add `og:title` and `og:image`, so a link shared on social media shows a preview.
formula: no og:title or og:image on the page

rule: The site is served over plain HTTP. Serve every page over HTTPS; browsers mark plain HTTP pages "Not secure".
formula: the site's origin is http://

rule: The http:// address doesn't move to https://. Redirect plain HTTP to HTTPS with a permanent redirect.
formula: http:// home page doesn't end on https://

rule: HTTPS pages that load files over plain HTTP. Load every image, script and stylesheet over HTTPS; browsers block or flag the rest.
formula: an https page references an http:// subresource

rule: Security headers missing on the home page. Send them from the server or CDN; each closes a common kind of attack.
formula: a header from the list missing on the home page (HSTS only on https; X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors)

rule: AI crawlers that robots.txt blocks. Nothing to fix if it's intended. A blocked assistant can't read or cite the site.
formula: robots.txt disallows the home page for an AI crawler on the list
notes: Information only: blocking AI crawlers can be a deliberate choice.

rule: Pages with almost no text until JavaScript runs. Send the main content in the HTML: crawlers that don't run JavaScript, many AI crawlers among them, see an empty page.
formula: visible text in the HTML < THIN_TEXT_CHARS and the page has scripts

rule: Links that appear only after JavaScript runs. Put important links in the HTML as `<a href>`: crawlers that don't run JavaScript can't follow the others.
formula: a same-site link in the rendered page that its HTML doesn't have
data_needed: the website, rendered in Chromium (a browser pass)
notes: Rendered pass only. The crawl then follows these links too, so the pages behind them are audited.

rule: No analytics tag found. Install analytics (for example GA4), or check it isn't loaded in a way this scan can't see.
formula: no analytics vendor in the HTML (or, rendered, in the requests)
notes: Without --render, a site whose only tag is a GTM container isn't flagged: the analytics inside it is invisible to the HTML.

rule: Tags that loaded but sent nothing during the scan. Open the page in your own browser and watch the network tab for the tag's requests. Common causes: a consent category that stays off after accepting, a broken ID or trigger, or a tag (Meta's, for one) that ignores automated browsers.
formula: a vendor's script loads but no hit request is seen before or after consent
data_needed: the website, rendered in Chromium (a browser pass)
notes: Rendered pass only.

rule: Tags that send data before the visitor consents. Hold them until consent, or use Consent Mode's cookieless pings, wherever privacy law (such as the GDPR) requires consent.
formula: an ads or analytics hit before consent, a consent banner present
data_needed: the website, rendered in Chromium (a browser pass)
notes: Rendered pass only. Consent Mode's cookieless pings (gcs with a denied state) are counted apart, as Google designed them for before consent.

rule: Tags send data and no consent banner was recognised. If you have visitors where consent is required (the EU, the UK and others), add a banner. If you have one, pass its accept button with `--consent-selector`.
formula: ads or analytics hits and no consent platform recognised
data_needed: the website, rendered in Chromium (a browser pass)
notes: Rendered pass only.

rule: A consent banner was found but couldn't be accepted. These results are the before-consent state only. Pass the accept button's CSS selector with `--consent-selector`.
formula: a consent platform recognised but its accept button not clicked
data_needed: the website, rendered in Chromium (a browser pass)
notes: Rendered pass only.

rule: Google tags run with no Consent Mode default. Set a default (`gtag('consent', 'default', ...)`) before the tags load, so Google can model the conversions of visitors who decline.
formula: Google tags, a consent banner, and no gtag consent command in dataLayer
data_needed: the website, rendered in Chromium (a browser pass)
notes: Rendered pass only. The account-side counterpart is meas-consent-mode.

rule: Third-party hosts this scan doesn't recognise. Check you know what each one is: any of them could be a tracker.
formula: a third-party host no signature matches
data_needed: the website, rendered in Chromium (a browser pass)
notes: Rendered pass only.

rule: Accessibility problem. See the axe rule's page for how to fix it; automated checks find only some problems.
formula: an axe-core violation of WCAG 2.0/2.1 A or AA; severity from axe's impact
data_needed: the website, rendered in Chromium (a browser pass)
notes: Rendered pass only. Automated checks find some problems, not all.

rule: Slow Largest Contentful Paint (lab). Make the biggest image or text block load sooner: compress it, preload it, cut render-blocking scripts.
formula: median lab LCP > LCP_GOOD_MS; high above LCP_POOR_MS
data_needed: the website, rendered in Chromium (a browser pass)
notes: Rendered pass only. Lab, not field data.

rule: Layout shifts while loading (lab). Reserve space for images, ads and embeds, so content doesn't jump.
formula: median lab CLS > CLS_GOOD; high above CLS_POOR
data_needed: the website, rendered in Chromium (a browser pass)
notes: Rendered pass only. Lab, not field data.

rule: Main thread blocked while loading (lab). Ship less JavaScript, split long tasks, and defer what isn't needed at load.
formula: median lab TBT > TBT_GOOD_MS; high above TBT_POOR_MS
data_needed: the website, rendered in Chromium (a browser pass)
notes: Rendered pass only. TBT stands in for INP, which needs real visitors' clicks.

rule: Real visitors wait for the main content. Chrome's field data says the biggest element loads slowly for real phone visitors: compress and preload it, and cut render-blocking files.
formula: whole-site p75 LCP for phones > 2500 ms; high above 4000 ms
notes: Needs your own Google API key. Field data, the numbers Google's ranking signal uses.

rule: Real visitors' taps and clicks respond slowly. Chrome's field data says the page is slow to react to input: ship less JavaScript and break up long tasks.
formula: whole-site p75 INP for phones > 200 ms; high above 500 ms
notes: Needs your own Google API key.

rule: Real visitors see the layout jump. Chrome's field data says content shifts while visitors read: reserve space for images, ads and embeds.
formula: whole-site p75 CLS for phones > 0.1; high above 0.25
notes: Needs your own Google API key.

rule: Each area (SEO, links, indexing and so on) starts at 100 and every finding in it costs points by severity: high 20, medium 10, low 4, info none. Grades: A from 90, B from 80, C from 70, D from 60, F below. No scores for an inconclusive scan.
formula: 100 - sum of the findings' points
notes: Our own weights, written down so they can be argued with. The report shows what each finding cost.

rule: A scan too broken to judge the site by is inconclusive: bot protection blocked it, robots.txt couldn't be read, the start page didn't load, or a quarter of the pages (from 4 fetched) gave no answer. With --fail-on it exits 4, never a pass.
Bot protection blocked the scan. Allow the `OpenPPC-SiteAudit` user agent in your bot protection and run again. Nothing else was checked.
formula: the start page is a bot-protection challenge

rule: The crawl is polite by default: 2 requests at a time, half a second apart, a robots.txt Crawl-delay honoured up to 10 seconds, and a 429 or 503 retried once after Retry-After (up to 30 seconds). --fast lifts the pause and runs 8 at a time.

No page limit by default; URL patterns are capped instead, so endless calendars and filters end: 500 URLs per path pattern and 10 query-string variants per path. Every skipped URL is counted in the report.

Limits per response: 5 MB of body after decompression, 15 s to connect or between bytes, 30 s in all, 10 redirects; robots.txt read to 500 KiB as Google does; sitemaps to the protocol's 50 MB, 50 files.
threshold: 5 MB; 15 s; 30 s; 10; 500 KiB; 50 MB; 50 files

rule: --render loads the home page and one page per section (5 by default) in Chromium, and measures Web Vitals on the home page (--vitals-pages for more) as the median of 3 loads on a Moto G Power screen with Lighthouse's mobile throttling as DevTools applies it: 4x CPU slowdown, 562.5 ms latency, 1.44 Mbps down, 675 Kbps up. A load still going after 45 seconds is measured as it is then, as Lighthouse does. A rough estimate: Lighthouse's own score simulates throttling instead.
threshold: 5 pages; 3 runs; 4x; 562.5 ms; 1474.56 Kbps; 675 Kbps; 1 page; 45 s

rule: With --psi, the Performance area is PageSpeed Insights' speed score for the start page on a phone, 0 to 100 as pagespeed.web.dev shows it, graded like the other areas; Performance findings then cost no points of their own. PSI's colours: green from 90, orange from 50, red below.
formula: Lighthouse's score: log-normal metric scores weighted FCP 10, SI 10, LCP 25, TBT 30, CLS 25
notes: Without --psi, Performance keeps points per finding from lab loads on this computer, labelled a rough estimate.

rule: --psi measures the start page and each --render-url page, at most 5, on a phone and a desktop, 2 calls at a time, waiting up to 120 seconds each. It refuses --allow-private, a page that isn't public, and an address carrying a secret-looking value, before anything is sent.

Lighthouse's Performance category as PageSpeed Insights reports it: its score and each audit, listed in the report's All Lighthouse audits section under Lighthouse's own name and never graded as an OpenPPC finding. The parity matrix (lab/lighthouse-13.csv) places each audit and names the OpenPPC rule that checks the same thing.
notes: One row per Lighthouse category, not per audit: a recorded exception. The matrix's test checks every audit in the fixtures is placed.

rule: Lighthouse's Accessibility category as PageSpeed Insights reports it: its score and each audit, listed in the report's All Lighthouse audits section under Lighthouse's own name and never graded as an OpenPPC finding. The parity matrix (lab/lighthouse-13.csv) places each audit and names the OpenPPC rule that checks the same thing.
notes: One row per Lighthouse category, not per audit: a recorded exception. The matrix's test checks every audit in the fixtures is placed.

The parity matrix (lab/lighthouse-13.csv) places each audit and names the OpenPPC rule that checks the same thing.
notes: One row per Lighthouse category, not per audit: a recorded exception. The matrix's test checks every audit in the fixtures is placed.

rule: Lighthouse's SEO category as PageSpeed Insights reports it: its score and each audit, listed in the report's All Lighthouse audits section under Lighthouse's own name and never graded as an OpenPPC finding. The parity matrix (lab/lighthouse-13.csv) places each audit and names the OpenPPC rule that checks the same thing.
notes: One row per Lighthouse category, not per audit: a recorded exception. The matrix's test checks every audit in the fixtures is placed.

rule: Lighthouse's Agentic Browsing category as PageSpeed Insights reports it: its score and each audit, listed in the report's All Lighthouse audits section under Lighthouse's own name and never graded as an OpenPPC finding. The parity matrix (lab/lighthouse-13.csv) places each audit and names the OpenPPC rule that checks the same thing.
notes: One row per Lighthouse category, not per audit: a recorded exception. The matrix's test checks every audit in the fixtures is placed.

rule: The Core Web Vitals assessment, as PageSpeed Insights gives it: passed when LCP, INP and CLS are all good at p75 (the line itself is good), LCP and CLS alone when INP has no data, none without LCP or CLS. With --psi it is PSI's own verdict; with --crux it is worked out the same way. The page's data comes first, the whole site's when the page has too few visitors.
formula: p75 <= good line for each Core Web Vital present

rule: --single checks the start page and any --render-url pages only: no sitemap, no missing-page probe, no llms.txt, no links followed or checked. The rules that need the whole site don't run.

Ad click IDs that a server redirect drops. Make the redirect keep the query string, or use the page it ends on as the ad's final URL. Without the click ID, the ad platform can't tie a sale or lead to the click that brought it.
formula: the start page fetched with each parameter set to OPENPPC-TEST ends, after a server redirect, on a URL without that value
notes: Server redirects only: a redirect in JavaScript, or a page script that rewrites the address, isn't seen yet. The site's logs and CRM may record the test value.
